measure_note: central dip, not the pre-registered saddle-between-outermost-maxima: the pre-registered index is degenerate on a unimodal profile (the control read 0.047, no headroom) because the outermost local maxima land on the shoulders of the same hump. The replacement was made after the fields were dumped and before any pair number was read; the control check is unchanged.
verdict: NOT REPORTABLE AS PRE-REGISTERED, WITH AN AUXILIARY NUMBER. The pre-registered bimodality index fails its own control (the single body reads 0.05 because its cross-section is an annulus), so the pre-registered question is unanswered. An auxiliary and not pre-registered measurement of the body's WIDTH at the midpoint between the parents' positions gives a median waist ratio of 0.357 at steps 50-120: after the two components have merged the body is a dumbbell with a bridge four to five cells wide against lobes of ten to fourteen. So the field does not relax into a round blob while it lasts, but the pattern fades inside 300 steps, and a dumbbell that never has time to relax is not the same claim as a preserved seam.

neck_measure.definition: at the midpoint between the two parent positions, the extent of the body above threshold 0.2 along the perpendicular axis, divided by the same extent through the lobes; a dumbbell has a ratio well below 1, a single round blob has nothing to compare and reads >= 1
neck_measure.why: the pre-registered central-dip index has no headroom: a body's cross-section is an annulus, so a single body has a central dip too and the control reads 0.05 instead of ~0.9
neck_measure.field_decay: the peak falls from 0.75 at step 10 to 0.02 at step 300 in both arms
